questions.stem: A 4-bit binary counter holds 0111. What does it hold after counting up by one?
questions.explain: 0111 is 7 and 7 + 1 = 8, which is 1000. The three low 1s turn to 0 and the carry flips the next bit.

questions.stem: How many bits are needed to give each of 10 states its own binary code?
questions.explain: 3 bits give only 8 codes, but 4 bits give 16, which is enough for 10 states.

questions.stem: A truth table lists every case of 3 true/false variables. How many rows does it have?
questions.explain: Each variable has 2 cases, so the table has 2 × 2 × 2 = 8 rows.

questions.stem: A 3-to-8 decoder receives the input 101. Which output line is 1? (The outputs are numbered 0 to 7.)
questions.explain: A decoder raises exactly one output, the one whose number equals the input. 101 is 5, so output 5 is high.
